So the count is ONE STRAND PER HImode->SImode WIDENING SITE, and our body has two sites; the Group A spec is therefore 'the arithmetic must contain four widening sites', not 'declare more locals'. sessions.lever: the named real-s16-quantity family (clamp-limit carriers, clamped-dimension locals, natural w/h idiom)
sessions.note: THE NAMED FAMILY DOES NOT DELIVER GROUP A, but the round produced the single most useful fact so far. Six variants, every local REAL (holding a value the body already computes and uses): the two clamp limits as s16 locals used by both the compare and the clamping assignment; the same hoisted to the top of the body; the clamped height as an s16 local feeding both the store and the shift; the natural w/h dimension-local clamp idiom with control flow preserved; and three combinations. All but one hold at exactly 2 orphans / 142 insns / score 47. THE EXCEPTION IS THE HANDLE: `lim_top` (both clamp globals read once into s16 xlim/ylim at the top, used by both compares) gives orphans=1, vars=8, frame=56 AT THE SAME 142 INSTRUCTIONS (score 55), reproduced. That refutes any 'vars is stuck at 16' reading - the strand count DOES move with source shape, just downward so far. Mechanistically, hoisting the load away from its compare REMOVED a strand, so a strand requires the widening to sit where combine cannot fold it into the load; the next session should work that lever in reverse. TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS on any candidate, both derived from target: the multiply must keep RE-READING arg0->x from memory (target splice regfix.txt:3417 is `lh $3,4($17)` ... `mult $3,$2`), and target emits the same two `sll ,0x10` + one `sra ,0x10` we do, so the two extra strands must be widenings combine folds away entirely. DISCIPLINE: no synthetic-strand spelling was tried and none should be - nothing reaches 3 or 4 orphans by any means, real or not, so there is no 'only works with a semantically empty local' trade-off to adjudicate. Banked on measurement, not on a policy call. src/display.c reverted.

sessions.lever: reverse-lim_top: RTL census of widening SITES per pass (tmp/widen.py) -- reframes Group A entirely
sessions.note: MECHANISM CORRECTION - THE SITE COUNT WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM. tmp/widen.py censuses HImode->SImode widening pairs per pass. The body ALREADY HAS FIVE (flow pass: pseudos 83, 89, 96, 100, 109); combine folds all five and only TWO (96, 100) leave an orphan. So rounds 1-6 were adding and removing SITES, a quantity that was never short, which is exactly why 25 variants moved nothing. There are three outcomes per site and only the middle one buys a frame slot: (a) combine merges cleanly with a single-use intermediate -> no instructions and NO SLOT (base sites 83, 89, 109); (b) combine merges but the intermediate is MULTI-USE so it preserves a (use) insn -> 8-BYTE SLOT (base 96, 100); (c) combine cannot merge -> real sll+sra emitted, no slot (lim_top's 90, 99). That is combine.c:1458 `added_sets_2 = !dead_or_set_p(i3, i2dest)`, the same mechanism packed-multiply-cluster documents. THE REAL SPEC IS THEREFORE: make two of the three cleanly-folding sites (83, 89, 109) MULTI-USE - some `X << 16` must be read by a second consumer besides its own `>> 16` - NOT 'find more s16 quantities'. This also explains lim_top's 2->1: it did not lose a site, it pushed sites 90/99 into outcome (c), which emits real shifts and no slot, hence score 55 at the same 142 instructions. Screening constraint for any candidate: the new multi-use must not push a site into outcome (c), because the visible sll/sll/sra census must stay identical. src/display.c reverted.
